import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows strong association with outcome
    # Use Welch's t-test for continuous features, chi-square for others
    drivers = []
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # Calculate effect sizes and p-values for all features
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        x = feats.x[:, i]
        y = feats.y
        if feats.types[i] in ('expression', 'copy_number'):
            # Welch's t-test for continuous variables
            group0 = x[y == 0]
            group1 = x[y == 1]
            if len(group0) > 1 and len(group1) > 1:
                t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
                effect_size = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
            else:
                effect_size = 0
                p_val = 1
        else:
            # For categorical/clinical features, use mutual information
            effect_size = mutual_info_classif(x.reshape(-1, 1), y)[0]
            p_val = 0.05  # Placeholder - mutual info doesn't give p-value directly
        
        effect_sizes.append((effect_size, p_val, fid))
    
    # Sort by effect size (absolute value)
    effect_sizes.sort(key=lambda x: abs(x[0]), reverse=True)
    
    # Check for near-duplicates and select top features
    selected_features = set()
    for _, _, fid in effect_sizes:
        if len(selected_features) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
            break
        # Skip if too correlated with already selected features
        is_duplicate = False
        for selected_fid in selected_features:
            col1 = feats.column(selected_fid)
            col2 = feats.column(fid)
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1], feats.x[:, col2])[0, 1]) >= 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        if not is_duplicate:
            selected_features.add(fid)
    
    # Select features that show strong association with outcome
    # Look for features with large effect size (|effect_size| > 0.3) and low p-value (< 0.05)
    significant_features = [(abs(effect), p, fid) for effect, p, fid in effect_sizes if abs(effect) > 0.3 and p < 0.05]
    significant_features.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # If we have strong signals, select those as drivers
    if significant_features:
        drivers = [fid for _, _, fid in significant_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
        columns = list(selected_features)
        
        # Add some interaction terms between top features
        top_features = [fid for _, _, fid in significant_features[:3]]
        for i in range(len(top_features)):
            for j in range(i+1, len(top_features)):
                products.append((top_features[i], top_features[j]))
        
        # Assign weights based on effect sizes
        for fid in selected_features:
            idx = feats.column(fid)
            x = feats.x[:, idx]
            y = feats.y
            if feats.types[idx] in ('expression', 'copy_number'):
                group0 = x[y == 0]
                group1 = x[y == 1]
                if len(group0) > 1 and len(group1) > 1:
                    effect = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
                    loadings[fid] = effect
                else:
                    loadings[fid] = 0
            else:
                # For non-continuous features, use mutual info as proxy
                loadings[fid] = mutual_info_classif(x.reshape(-1, 1), y)[0]
    else:
        # No strong mechanisms found
        drivers = ()
        columns = list(selected_features)
    
    # Ensure we don't exceed MAX_DRIVERS for drivers
    drivers = drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=tuple(columns), products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
